headline: Clay casting, edible treasure hunts and community adventures
summary: Bristol discoveries for 12–13 September, with community gardens, clay casting and small local festivals. Weekday library sessions and clearly labelled backups are available too.

datedPicks.title: Last weekend of the Aardman detective trail
datedPicks.location: Bristol Museum & Art Gallery, Queens Road, Bristol BS8 1RL
datedPicks.description: A free map-led hunt for Aardman objects in the galleries during its final week.
datedPicks.ageSuitability: Organiser: families and curious explorers of all ages. DoNext fit: ages 4–12 following a map, with younger children helped by an adult.
datedPicks.appeal: Collect a detective map and track down tiny Aardman treasures hidden around the museum.
datedPicks.parentTip: This free trail is at Bristol Museum & Art Gallery, not the separate M Shed exhibition. It ends 13 September; pick up the map at the museum.

datedPicks.appeal: Turn a story or poem into a LEGO model to display in the library.
datedPicks.parentTip: Free drop-in; an adult must accompany the child. The council lists 8 and 22 September.

datedPicks.description: Librarian-led nursery rhymes and songs for babies and toddlers (0–3; storytime suit 1–4). All-year Saturday session; older siblings welcome.
datedPicks.ageSuitability: Organiser: rhyme sessions suit ages 0–3; storytime suits ages 1–4. Older siblings are welcome.
datedPicks.appeal: Share familiar nursery rhymes and songs with a librarian and other young families.
datedPicks.parentTip: Free, no booking needed. Starts 10:45 and lasts around 20 minutes; arrive for the start.

datedPicks.title: Clay, casting and a potter’s wheel
datedPicks.location: Spike Island, 133 Cumberland Road, Bristol BS1 6UX
datedPicks.cost: Adult £3 · children free · materials provided; check booking fees
datedPicks.ageSuitability: Organiser: all ages and abilities with adult supervision. DoNext fit: makers aged 5–12; younger children need hands-on help.
datedPicks.description: Make clay forms by hand, with moulds or on a potter’s wheel, then explore plaster casting with art fabricators.
datedPicks.appeal: Try real sculpture-making: shape the clay, make a mould, explore a plaster cast. A hands-on workshop with materials supplied.
datedPicks.parentTip: Book ahead and check availability. Children must stay with an adult; wear clothes that can get messy.

datedPicks.title: Potions and puppets at the farm’s birthday
datedPicks.location: Windmill Hill City Farm, Philip Street, Bedminster, Bristol BS3 4EA
datedPicks.cost: Adult early bird £7.60 including fee · under-16 early bird advertised £4; check current child total
datedPicks.ageSuitability: Organiser: no age restrictions. Children attend with their grown-ups.
datedPicks.description: The city farm’s 50th anniversary brings puppet shows, animal tours, potion making, nature activities and live music.
datedPicks.appeal: A special birthday programme with potion making, puppet shows and animal tours across a working community farm.
datedPicks.parentTip: Activities are included; food and drink cost extra. Check current adult and child prices before booking, including the rule for babies.

datedPicks.title: A secret garden and a curious old dairy
datedPicks.location: Blaise Dairy Garden, Henbury Road, Bristol BS10 7QS
datedPicks.cost: Free estate entry; no separate garden charge listed
datedPicks.description: Explore the usually tucked-away Dairy Garden, its amphitheatre and historic dairy during a special opening.
datedPicks.ageSuitability: DoNext fit: curious ages 5–12 with an adult; no organiser age range or children’s workshop is advertised.
datedPicks.appeal: Find a small amphitheatre and an unusual old dairy, with volunteers ready for curious questions.
datedPicks.parentTip: Bring a picnic. The Community Garden Art Show is also on at the estate; check signs for the dairy entrance.

datedPicks.title: Art club at Filton Library
datedPicks.location: Filton Library, South Gloucestershire
datedPicks.description: Free monthly arts and crafts for ages 7–11; adult must accompany. Second Saturday of the month drop-in.
datedPicks.ageSuitability: Organiser: ages 7–11 only; an adult must accompany the child.
datedPicks.appeal: A focused 45-minute art-and-craft session for children aged 7–11.
datedPicks.parentTip: Free drop-in on 12 September. Suitable for ages 7–11 within the broader filters; adults must stay.

datedPicks.title: Steam along the harbour behind Henbury
datedPicks.location: M Shed, Princes Wharf, Wapping Road, Bristol BS1 4RN
datedPicks.cost: Paid tickets on the day · current adult/child fares not published
datedPicks.description: Steam rides on Bristol Harbour Railway behind locomotive Henbury along the quayside between M Shed and SS Great Britain — volunteer-run heritage railway.
datedPicks.statusNote: Volunteer-operated — crew, weather or mechanical issues can cancel. Call 0117 352 6600 to confirm before travel. Exact fares not listed on the organiser page.
datedPicks.ageSuitability: Organiser lists this as a family activity. DoNext fit: children who enjoy steam engines, with an adult.
datedPicks.appeal: Ride a real Bristol-built steam locomotive along the working harbour railway.
datedPicks.parentTip: Call 0117 352 6600 before travelling: volunteer crews, machinery or weather can change services. Last ride and fares are not published.

datedPicks.title: Tiny Planet: puppets, folk songs and a miniature world
datedPicks.location: the egg, Theatre Royal Bath, 36 Monmouth Street, Bath BA1 2AN
datedPicks.cost: £11–£14 per ticket including fees · one adult + one child £22–£28
datedPicks.description: Puppet theatre with live folk song and camera projection: a whole world no bigger than a house. Distinctive family show for ages 5+ — book ahead for weekend slots.
datedPicks.ageSuitability: Organiser: ages 5+. DoNext fit: children who enjoy imaginative puppet theatre.
datedPicks.appeal: Watch a house-sized planet come alive through puppets, live folk music and camera projections.
datedPicks.parentTip: This is in central Bath. Allow for your journey and book the exact performance; each show lasts 55 minutes without an interval.

datedPicks.title: Garden games, music and face painting
datedPicks.location: Redcatch Community Garden, Redcatch Park, Broad Walk, Knowle, Bristol BS4 2RD
datedPicks.cost: Adult £4 · child £6 · one adult + child £10 before any booking fees
datedPicks.ageSuitability: Organiser: all ages welcome in the noon–6pm session.
datedPicks.description: Redcatch’s first RCG Fest has music, cabaret, face painting and funfair games, with a drink included in the ticket.
datedPicks.appeal: A community-garden festival where games, face painting, the show and a drink are included in the ticket.
datedPicks.parentTip: Choose the family session, which ends at 18:00. Food costs extra. Ask about baby tickets; the later session is adults only.
